answer: A farm that wants 55 keys hence pays 55 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the violet seed, the trellis timing is verifiable from the sable record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 352 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is inexpensive once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
